research_question: What is the effect of statins compared with placebo or no statin treatment on end-of-treatment proteinuria in adults with chronic kidney disease not requiring dialysis?
outcome_description: Urinary protein excretion in grams per 24 hours (g/24 h) at the end of treatment (or 24-hour urinary albumin excretion if protein excretion is not reported)
positive_direction: A positive effect size indicates lower proteinuria (reduced 24-hour urinary protein excretion) favoring statin therapy over control
search_queries: statin chronic kidney disease proteinuria randomized trial
HMG-CoA reductase inhibitor CKD urinary protein excretion clinical trial
atorvastatin pravastatin non-dialysis CKD proteinuria controlled study
inclusion_criteria: Adults with chronic kidney disease not requiring renal replacement therapy (dialysis or kidney transplant)
Randomized controlled trial or clinical study comparing statin monotherapy to placebo or no statin control
Quantitative reporting of urinary protein excretion (or urinary albumin excretion) at the end of the treatment period
exclusion_criteria: Not an original empirical study (systematic reviews, meta-analyses, editorials, commentaries, and animal/in vitro studies)
Studies conducted in dialysis-dependent patients or kidney transplant recipients
No comparison between a statin and placebo or untreated control (e.g., head-to-head statin comparisons or statin vs another active agent)
No quantitative end-of-treatment proteinuria or urinary protein/albumin excretion data extractable to compute mean difference
moderators_to_extract: Specific statin agent and daily dose/intensity
Underlying CKD etiology (diabetic vs non-diabetic CKD)
Baseline renal function (eGFR or CKD stage)
effect_size_note: Pool as mean difference (MD) in g/24 h using end-of-treatment values from the final on-treatment timepoint. Convert mg/24 h to g/24 h by dividing by 1000. Convert SE to SD using SD = SE * sqrt(n).
